notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
A two-level shelf surface over a wide base with drawers below — shown with books — but **load rating cannot be verified in this system**.

**Load rating disclaimer:** The configurator checks only geometry/fit (mesh clashes, joint bolts). It knows nothing about materials, print settings, strength, stiffness, creep or fastener pull-out. The parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material. Any claim to hold 50 kg would be untested. Safe use would require engineering analysis and physical testing, and treating the plastic build as display/light-duty storage only.

Build completed for demonstration: 3 top covers form a continuous deck (f22) for books, with two half-base bays fitted with notch drawers on opposite sides, joints locked.
